findings.reason: The protected Python solution precomputes a hash map mapping each word to a sorted list of its 0-based indices during initialization. For each query, it uses a two-pointer merge over the two sorted index lists to find the minimum absolute difference. The construction runs in O(n) time and each query takes O(k1 + k2) time where k1, k2 are occurrence counts. The solution is optimal; no candidate is required.

Scanning two sorted index lists with two pointers by advancing the pointer with the smaller value guarantees evaluating all candidate minimum distances, since advancing the larger pointer could only increase the difference.

Initialization takes O(n) time and O(n) space for storing all word-index postings lists. Each shortest query takes O(k1 + k2) <= O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
WordDistance class initializes with wordsDict (List[str]) and implements shortest(word1: str, word2: str) -> int according to the problem contract.

The approach accurately details precomputed posting-list index maps, two-pointer list-merging search, and O(n) preprocessing / O(k1 + k2) query bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover full-dictionary rescanning performance penalties, Cartesian product pair comparisons, frequent word occurrence lists, and distinct query word guarantees.
